title: Argentina Update — May 31, 2026
summary: The IMF approved Argentina's second program review on May 21, releasing $1 billion and projecting 3.5% GDP growth for 2026 as annual inflation fell to 32.4% (April). Central bank reserves reached a seven-year high on May 27, allowing Milei to ease peso exchange controls. Vaca Muerta shale production hit a record 874,000 bbl/day (February 2026) while an LNG export FID is targeted for H2 2026. Politically, Milei's approval rating rebounded from its lowest point ahead of October midterm elections, but disability funding cuts drew international criticism and journalists were injured covering retirees' weekly protests outside Congress.

title: Argentina: 490 Years of History Update — Thu May 28, 2026
summary: Bloomberg reported a recovery in President Milei's approval rating from its lowest point, tied to slowly easing inflation concerns ahead of the October 26, 2026 midterm elections. The Washington Post reported that the Milei government cut therapy and support funding for an estimated 5 million Argentines with disabilities as part of broader fiscal austerity measures. Photographer Antonio Becerra from Tiempo Argentino was injured by tear gas fired by federal security forces during the weekly retirees' protest in front of the National Congress in Buenos Aires.

title: Argentina: 490 Years of History Update — Wed May 27, 2026
summary: Argentina's central bank reserves reached their highest level since 2019, giving the Milei government room to further loosen exchange controls on the peso.

title: Argentina: 490 Years of History Update — Thu May 21, 2026
summary: IMF Approves Second Review of $20B Program, Releases $1 Billion Disbursement. Photographer Tomás Cuesta was beaten by police and arrested while covering an anti-austerity demonstration in Buenos Aires on May 21.
